title: Many Qubits
intro: What changes when there is more than one qubit: state spaces multiply, states can be entangled, a part of a system has to be described by a density matrix, and interactions between spins define the Hamiltonians quantum reservoirs are made of.

blocks.text: A quantum reservoir is a register of interacting qubits. This topic takes the single-qubit picture of the previous topics to many qubits, and ends where the QRC shelf's Open Quantum Systems Toolkit (#/qrc/open-systems) begins.

items: Composite Systems and Tensor Products (#/quantum/many-body/composite-systems): how qubits combine, the basis ordering every simulator uses, operators on one qubit of many, and the exponential growth of the state space.
Entanglement and Reduced States (#/quantum/many-body/entanglement): Bell states, the Schmidt decomposition, the partial trace and entanglement entropy.
Mixed States (#/quantum/many-body/mixed-states): the density matrix as the description of a system you do not fully know or only partly see, and why every reservoir is in a mixed state.
Spin Models (#/quantum/many-body/spin-models): Ising, transverse-field Ising, XX and Heisenberg Hamiltonians, and the disordered all-to-all model QRC uses.
M. A. Nielsen and I. L. Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information, 10th anniversary edition, Cambridge University Press (2010), chapter 2
J. Preskill, Lecture Notes for Physics 219: Quantum Information and Computation, Caltech (online), chapters 2 and 3
